summary.headline: iValue Q2 FY27 gross sales fell 17.6% YoY to INR 731.6 crores on a high base; management reiterates ~20% FY27 top-line and PAT growth guidance.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 gross sales rose 14% QoQ to INR 731.6 crores but fell 17.6% YoY against a base that included a roughly INR 150 crore large deal in Q2 FY26. H1 gross sales were INR 1,372.8 crores, down 8.1%, while H1 PAT fell 2.4% to INR 39.1 crores. Q2 results were flattered by a one-time high-margin deal and a INR 3.7 crore land-sale gain, and hit by a INR 4.4 crore receivable write-off from a single Indian partner. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% growth in top line and PAT, citing a tracked pipeline of INR 6,900 crores (up from INR 6,149 crores QoQ) and October billings that already exceed the full Q3 FY26 figure.

segments.name: Cybersecurity (largest, ~48% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 sales down 8.7% YoY. Management cites large-deal timing and customer budget deferrals; DPDP-related deals are being signed.

segments.name: Data center infrastructure (~19% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 growth of 39.7% YoY; budgets reportedly shifting from ILM toward DCI.

segments.name: Information lifecycle management (ILM, ~14% of H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: H1 sales down 48.1% YoY, driven by deferral of deals from one large OEM into Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: ALM, cloud and others (~19% of H1 revenue)

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 guidance reiterated as directional: ~20% top-line growth and ~20% PAT growth over FY26; management says it will narrow guidance at the Q3 call.
Management assumes an H1:H2 split of 40:60, implying full-year gross sales of about INR 3,430 crores and H2 of about INR 2,000 crores (~50% growth over H1).
Gross margin for FY27 expected around the current ~9% level or slightly above; medium-term net gross margin band of 9% to 9.5%, with overall margin between 9% and 10%.
Around 70% of incremental gross margin expected to flow to EBITDA, supporting an EBITDA margin expansion of about 20 to 25 bps in the medium term.
Annuity share of gross sales expected to end FY27 near 50% (plus or minus 1%), with absolute annuity sales rising in H2.
Capital allocation decision (acquisition, dividend, buyback or bonus) to follow if no acquisition target is found in FY27, likely at Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex plans were discussed on the call.

International push: ASEAN engagement (Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam) and CLM region through OEM and ecosystem partners; headcount added in ASEAN, worth about INR 1 to 1.5 crores of the H1 manpower increase.
Cloud: partnered with one hyperscaler and running a dedicated motion for hybrid workload migration, with results expected in coming quarters.
Manpower cost H1 FY27 INR 40.9 crores vs INR 35.5 crores in H1 FY26 (+15%), driven by new hires, ASEAN investment and 8-10% appraisals from 1 July.
demand_pricing: Large deals are defined as above INR 100 crores; the company typically wins 2 to 3 a year and is working on 5 to 6 large deals currently, with some at L1 stage and none lost.
Pipeline INR 6,900 crores vs INR 6,149 crores last quarter (~12% QoQ). Billings for October plus bookings convertible in the quarter already exceed full Q3 FY26 billings.

Customers are delaying awards by 2 to 3 months and negotiating heavily with SIs after L1 selection, citing hardware and component price inflation. Some customers are opting for renewals over tech refresh, boosting annuity renewals.
Margin pressure from OEM price negotiations is present but has been limited so far, per management.
OEM consolidation has occurred, but no revenue or margin hit so far; the company has signed other OEMs in the same space and has a funnel running.
A customer default by an Indian partner led to a INR 4.4 crore write-off after a settlement; the Q2 one-time gain of INR 3.7 crores came from sale of vacant land (non-operating income).

qa_highlights.question: Early indicators for Q3, and what would the Q3 colour look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited large deals moving closer to conversion and October billings plus next two months' convertible bookings already exceeding full Q3 FY26 billings, with about 45 days left in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 20% guidance need INR 600-700 crores per quarter, and is it large-deal led or higher conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large deals are binary, so a 6-month conversion rate can look above 35%; annuity share should fall to about 50% by year-end as large and net new deals land in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H2 guidance imply ~50% growth, and is it confident?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; applying the 40:60 H1:H2 ratio to H1 sales of INR 1,372 crores gives FY27 of about INR 3,430 crores and H2 of about INR 2,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why was non-annuity sales only about INR 295 crores in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are negotiating after award and extending renewals to preserve budget for other spend, which shifted mix toward annuity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 28% in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 manpower cost rose 15% to INR 40.9 crores, from new hires for growth, ASEAN investment (INR 1 to 1.5 crores) and 8-10% appraisals.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of forex on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Payables are hedged, but a mark-to-market impact of about INR 1 crore hit P&L in the period as of 30 September.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cybersecurity incidents lift demand, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees an uptick but expects the benefit mainly in FY28, as customers are unlikely to change budgets mid-year; deferred tech refreshes are also expected to come through.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the DPDP opportunity and will local OEMs be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marquee DPDP deals are already signed, with more opportunities in Q3 and Q4, and it expects Indian OEMs to be a large part of the opportunity.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on a small number of large Q3 and Q4 deals; any slippage from 31 March to 1 April-type timing would shift the quarter.
Gross margin pressure from OEM and SI price negotiations and hardware cost inflation; normalised Q2 margin 8.9% vs reported 9.6%.
ILM decline of 48.1% in H1 depends on the large OEM's deals moving into Q3 and Q4.
Further OEM consolidation could hit revenue; management has not seen an impact yet.
Other expenses rose about 35% YoY including the write-off; management says ~15-18% excluding it. Watch for further partner credit issues.
Watch Q3 FY27 results for conversion of the INR 6,900 crore pipeline, narrowing of guidance, and annuity share trend.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H2 and Q3 conversion while candid that H1 was weak; management repeatedly stressed deal timing and lumpiness and kept guidance directional. Answers on the cybersecurity-incident tailwind and the ILM decline were more qualitative, with few numbers.
key_quotes: We want to address this performance directly and put it in the right context.
As always, the funnel is not the same as booked business and conversion and execution will be critical.
We are giving a directional guidance of 20% growth in PAT and 20% growth in top line.

financial_highlights.value: 48 days; ROCE 24.7% (Q2), 22.9% (H1); cash net of debt INR 124 crores

growth.why: Management reiterated directional ~20% FY27 top-line and PAT growth, requiring about 50% H2 growth over H1 (H1 sales down 8.1%); backing is a INR 6,900 crore tracked pipeline and 5-6 large deals in progress, but no capacity additions, and the guidance is directional with narrowing deferred to Q3.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 gross margin around 9% (Q2 reported 9.6%, normalised ~8.9%) and medium-term EBITDA expansion of about 20-25 bps, with ~70% of incremental gross margin flowing to EBITDA, but OEM and SI price pressure and hardware inflation cut against it and H1 EBITDA margin was only 3.8%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management discussed no capacity or capex plans; ASEAN headcount add is worth only INR 1 to 1.5 crores of H1 manpower cost.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance needs H2 gross sales of about INR 2,000 crores, ~50% above H1's INR 1,372.8 crores (down 8.1% YoY), backed by a INR 6,900 crore pipeline and 5-6 large deals with none lost, but depends on Q3 and Q4 large-deal timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the only capital allocation comment is that an acquisition, dividend, buyback or bonus decision follows at Q1 FY28 if no target is found.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is held directional at ~20% FY27 top-line and PAT growth against H1 down 8.1%, and management will only narrow it at the Q3 call, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Full-year ~20% growth needs about 50% H2 growth over H1, and any slip of large deals from 31 March into 1 April or beyond would shift the quarter; the ILM decline of 48.1% also depends on one OEM's deals landing in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; cloud hybrid-migration motion and DPDP offerings were mentioned without launch dates.

rows.label: Q3 large-deal conversion from INR 6,900 crore pipeline
rows.why: October billings plus bookings convertible in the quarter already exceed full Q3 FY26 billings, with 5-6 large deals in progress (above INR 100 crores each), 2-3 won per year and none lost.

rows.label: DPDP-driven cybersecurity deals
rows.why: Marquee DPDP deals are already signed with more opportunities in Q3 and Q4, though the broader cybersecurity-incident demand benefit is expected mainly in FY28.

rows.label: Annuity share falling toward 50% of sales
rows.why: Annuity was 53.5% of H1 gross sales (INR 734.2 crores, +16.1% YoY) and management expects it near 50% (+/-1%) as net-new and large deals land in Q3 and Q4.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q3 and H2 conversion and the INR 6,900 crore pipeline, while candid that H1 was weak and kept guidance directional; the Q&A pressed on how the ~50% H2 step-up is achieved, and answers on the cybersecurity tailwind and ILM decline were qualitative with few numbers.
